syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Electric charge, conductors and insulators

concepts.learning_objective: Explain charging by rubbing as a transfer of electrons and predict attraction or repulsion between charged bodies.
Distinguish conductors from insulators by the mobility of their charges and explain how each holds charge.

topics.title: Basic properties of electric charge

concepts.learning_objective: Add the charges of a system algebraically, treating charge as a scalar.
Apply conservation of charge to redistribution and particle processes in an isolated system.
Use q = ne to relate the charge on a body to the number of electrons transferred.

topics.title: Coulomb's law

concepts.learning_objective: State Coulomb's law and the inverse-square dependence of the force on distance.
Calculate the electrostatic force between two point charges in vacuum.
Compare electric and gravitational forces between charged particles.

topics.title: Forces between multiple charges

concepts.learning_objective: State the superposition principle for forces between several point charges.
Find the net force on a charge due to several charges by vector addition.

topics.title: Electric field and electric field lines

concepts.learning_objective: Define electric field and calculate the field of a point charge and its effect on charged particles.
Interpret electric field lines and explain their general properties.

topics.title: Electric flux

concepts.learning_objective: Define electric flux as E.dS and calculate it for a flat surface in a uniform field.
Use the area vector and the outward-normal convention for closed surfaces.

topics.title: Electric dipole and dipole in an external field

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the dipole moment and compare the fields of a short dipole on its axis and equatorial plane.
Find the force and torque on a dipole in uniform and non-uniform electric fields.

topics.title: Continuous charge distribution, Gauss's law and its applications

concepts.learning_objective: Define linear, surface and volume charge densities with their units.
State Gauss's law and use it to find the flux through a closed surface.
Apply Gauss's law to find the field of an infinite line charge and of plane sheets of charge.

topics.title: Electrostatic potential and the potential of a point charge

concepts.learning_objective: Define electrostatic potential as work done per unit test charge and relate it to the conservative nature of the Coulomb force.
Calculate the potential due to a point charge using V = q/(4 pi epsilon0 r).

topics.title: Potential due to an electric dipole and a system of charges

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the potential of a dipole depends on distance and on the angle with the dipole axis.
Find the potential due to several point charges by algebraic addition of their potentials.

topics.title: Equipotential surfaces and the relation between field and potential

concepts.learning_objective: Identify equipotential surfaces and explain why the field is normal to them and no work is done along them.
Use E = -dV/dl to find the magnitude and direction of the electric field from potential values.

topics.title: Potential energy of a system of charges and in an external field

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the electrostatic potential energy of a system of point charges.
Apply U = qV to a charge moving in an external potential.
Use U = -p.E to find the potential energy of a dipole and the work needed to rotate it.

topics.title: Electrostatics of conductors, dielectrics and polarisation

concepts.learning_objective: State the electrostatic properties of a conductor: zero interior field, surface charge, constant potential and normal surface field.
Explain polar and non-polar molecules and how polarisation reduces the field inside a dielectric.

topics.title: Capacitors, the parallel plate capacitor and the effect of a dielectric

concepts.learning_objective: Define capacitance as C = Q/V and state its SI unit.
Calculate the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor using C = epsilon0 A/d.
Explain how a dielectric changes the capacitance, charge and potential difference of a capacitor.

topics.title: Combination of capacitors and energy stored in a capacitor

concepts.learning_objective: Find the equivalent capacitance and charges for capacitors in series and in parallel.
Calculate the energy stored in a capacitor and the energy changes when capacitors share charge.
Use u = (1/2) epsilon0 E^2 to find the energy density of an electric field.

topics.title: Electric current and currents in conductors

concepts.learning_objective: Define electric current as the rate of net charge flow across an area and use its SI unit.
Explain how an applied electric field turns the random motion of free charges into a steady current.

topics.title: Ohm's law, resistance and resistivity

concepts.learning_objective: Relate resistance to the length and cross-sectional area of a conductor through R = rho l / A.
Use resistivity, conductivity and current density in the form j = sigma E.

topics.title: Drift of electrons and the origin of resistivity

concepts.learning_objective: Derive and apply v_d = eE tau / m and I = n e A v_d for electrons in a metal.
Define mobility as drift speed per unit field and state its SI unit.

topics.title: Limitations of Ohm's law and resistivity of materials

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the ways in which devices such as diodes and GaAs deviate from Ohm's law.
Classify conductors, semiconductors and insulators by resistivity and its behaviour with temperature.
Apply rho_T = rho_0 [1 + alpha (T - T_0)] to find resistance at another temperature.

topics.title: Electrical energy and power

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate power dissipated in a resistor using P = VI = I^2 R = V^2 / R.
Explain why electrical power is transmitted at high voltage to reduce ohmic loss.

topics.title: Cells, emf, internal resistance and combinations of cells

concepts.learning_objective: Relate emf, terminal voltage and internal resistance through V = epsilon - I r.
Find the equivalent emf and internal resistance of cells in series and in parallel.

topics.title: Kirchhoff's rules and the Wheatstone bridge

concepts.learning_objective: Apply Kirchhoff's junction and loop rules and state the conservation laws behind them.
Use the balance condition of a Wheatstone bridge to find an unknown resistance.

topics.title: Magnetic force: Lorentz force and force on a current-carrying conductor

concepts.learning_objective: Apply F = q(v x B) to find the magnitude and direction of the magnetic force on a moving charge.
Use F = I l x B to find the force on a straight current-carrying conductor in a uniform magnetic field.

topics.title: Motion of a charged particle in a magnetic field

concepts.learning_objective: Derive and use r = mv/qB for a charge moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field.
Explain why the period is independent of speed and describe helical motion and its pitch.

topics.title: Biot-Savart law and field on the axis of a circular loop

concepts.learning_objective: State the Biot-Savart law and use it to find the magnitude and direction of the field of a current element.
Calculate the magnetic field at the centre and on the axis of a circular current loop.

topics.title: Ampere's circuital law and the solenoid

concepts.learning_objective: State Ampere's circuital law and apply it to find the field of a long straight wire.
Use B = mu0 n I for the field inside a long solenoid and describe the field outside it.

topics.title: Force between two parallel currents; the ampere

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the force per unit length between two long parallel currents and state whether it attracts or repels.
State the definition of the ampere in terms of the force between parallel conductors.

topics.title: Torque on a current loop; the magnetic dipole

concepts.learning_objective: Use tau = m x B to find the torque on a current loop in a uniform magnetic field.
Explain why a planar current loop behaves as a magnetic dipole of moment m = IA and use its far field.

topics.title: The moving coil galvanometer

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the working of a moving coil galvanometer and define its current and voltage sensitivity.
Calculate the shunt or series resistance needed to convert a galvanometer into an ammeter or voltmeter.

topics.title: The bar magnet and magnetic field lines

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the basic properties of magnetic poles, including the non-existence of isolated poles.
State and apply the properties of magnetic field lines of a bar magnet.

topics.title: Bar magnet as an equivalent solenoid

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a bar magnet can be treated as an equivalent current-carrying solenoid.
Calculate the magnetic moment of a solenoid and compare the far axial fields it produces.

topics.title: The dipole in a uniform magnetic field

concepts.learning_objective: Use tau = m x B to find the torque on a magnetic dipole in a uniform field.
Use U = -m.B to find potential energy, work done and equilibrium positions of a dipole.

topics.title: The electrostatic analog

concepts.learning_objective: Map the equations of an electric dipole onto those of a magnetic dipole.
Calculate the axial and equatorial fields of a short bar magnet and their directions.

topics.title: Magnetism and Gauss's law

concepts.learning_objective: State Gauss's law for magnetism and relate it to the absence of magnetic monopoles.
Judge whether a given field-line pattern can represent a static magnetic field.

topics.title: Magnetisation and magnetic intensity

concepts.learning_objective: Define magnetisation M and magnetic intensity H and use B = mu0 (H + M).
Relate susceptibility, relative permeability and permeability of a material.

topics.title: Magnetic properties of materials

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the behaviour and examples of diamagnetic substances, including superconductors.
Explain paramagnetism and the effect of field and temperature on magnetisation.
Explain ferromagnetism using domains and distinguish hard and soft ferromagnets.

topics.title: Experiments of Faraday and Henry

concepts.learning_objective: Explain from Faraday's experiments that relative motion between a magnet (or current-carrying coil) and a coil induces a current.
Explain how a changing current in a stationary coil induces a momentary current in a nearby stationary coil.

topics.title: Magnetic flux and Faraday's law of induction

concepts.learning_objective: Define magnetic flux as B.A = BA cos(theta) and state its SI unit.
Apply Faraday's law, emf = -N dPhi/dt, to calculate induced emf and current.

topics.title: Lenz's law and conservation of energy

concepts.learning_objective: Use Lenz's law to find the direction of an induced current or the polarity of an induced emf.
Explain Lenz's law as a consequence of the law of conservation of energy.

topics.title: Motional electromotive force

concepts.learning_objective: Derive and apply the motional emf Blv for a conductor moving in a uniform magnetic field.
Explain motional emf through the Lorentz force on the free charges of a moving conductor.
Calculate the emf (1/2)B omega R^2 across a rod rotating in a uniform magnetic field.

topics.title: Mutual inductance

concepts.learning_objective: Obtain and use the mutual inductance of two long co-axial solenoids and the equality M12 = M21.
Calculate the emf induced in one coil by a changing current in a neighbouring coil.

topics.title: Self-inductance and magnetic energy

concepts.learning_objective: Obtain and use the self-inductance of a long solenoid and the back emf -L dI/dt.
Calculate the energy (1/2)LI^2 stored in an inductor and relate it to the energy density B^2/2mu0.

topics.title: AC generator

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the construction and working principle of an ac generator.
Use emf = NBA omega sin(omega t) to find the peak and instantaneous emf of an ac generator.

topics.title: AC voltage applied to a resistor

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the phase relation between current and voltage in a resistor and why it heats up although the average current is zero.
Relate rms and peak values of alternating current and voltage and use them to find average power in a resistor.

topics.title: Representation of ac current and voltage by phasors

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret a phasor as a rotating vector whose length is the amplitude and whose vertical projection is the instantaneous value.
Explain why voltages that are out of phase must be combined using phasors rather than added algebraically.

topics.title: AC voltage applied to an inductor

concepts.learning_objective: Use X_L = omega L to find the current through a pure inductor and predict how it changes with frequency.
State that current lags voltage by pi/2 in a pure inductor and explain why the average power over a cycle is zero.

topics.title: AC voltage applied to a capacitor

concepts.learning_objective: Use X_C = 1/(omega C) to find the current through a capacitor and predict how it changes with frequency.
State that current leads voltage by pi/2 in a capacitor and that no average power is consumed by it.

topics.title: AC voltage applied to a series LCR circuit and resonance

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the impedance and current of a series LCR circuit using the phasor (impedance) diagram.
Find the resonant frequency of a series LCR circuit and analyse the current and voltages at resonance.

topics.title: Power in ac circuit: the power factor

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate average power as P = V I cos(phi) and explain the effect of power factor on transmission losses.
Explain wattless current and how a capacitor improves the power factor of an inductive load.

topics.title: Transformers

concepts.learning_objective: State that a transformer works on mutual induction and needs a changing magnetic flux.
Apply V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p and I_s/I_p = N_p/N_s and explain why power is transmitted at high voltage.
Identify the energy losses in a real transformer and how each is reduced.

topics.title: Displacement current and the Ampere-Maxwell law

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a time-varying electric field gives rise to a displacement current i_d = ε0 dΦE/dt that equals the conduction current in a charging capacitor.
State the Ampere-Maxwell law and explain how it restores consistency and symmetry between electric and magnetic laws.

topics.title: Sources of electromagnetic waves

concepts.learning_objective: Identify accelerated (oscillating) charges as the source of electromagnetic waves whose frequency equals the frequency of oscillation.
Recall the experimental work of Hertz, J.C. Bose and Marconi on producing and transmitting electromagnetic waves.

topics.title: Nature of electromagnetic waves

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the mutually perpendicular orientation of E, B and the direction of propagation in a plane electromagnetic wave.
Use the relations ω = ck, νλ = c and B0 = E0/c to analyse a plane electromagnetic wave.
Relate the speed of electromagnetic waves to μ0, ε0 in vacuum and to μ, ε in a material medium.

topics.title: Electromagnetic spectrum: radio waves, microwaves and infrared

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that regions of the electromagnetic spectrum differ in wavelength or frequency and are classified by production and detection.
Describe the frequency bands, production and uses of radio waves and microwaves.
Explain why infrared waves are called heat waves and their role in the greenhouse effect.

topics.title: Visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the range of visible light and the sources, effects and absorption of ultraviolet radiation.
Describe the production, wavelength ranges and uses of X-rays and gamma rays.
Match each type of electromagnetic wave with its typical production method and detector (Table 8.1).
